title: The Share Rebilled on a Dispute Resolved Against the Cardholder, by Certificate Relationship
content:
The share rebilled on a card under Personal Credit Cards is read from the cardholder's holdings under Certificates of Deposit together with whether any card payment has been returned on that card account.

1. Where the cardholder holds an active certificate whose principal balance is at least 10000.00 USD and no card payment has been returned on this card account in the last twelve months, the rebilled share is 100 percent.

2. Where the cardholder holds an active certificate whose principal balance is below 10000.00 USD and no card payment has been returned on this card account in the last twelve months, the rebilled share is 90 percent.

3. Where neither of those holds, no adjustment to the rebilled share is made.

**The two parts in combination.**

| Active certificate principal | Card payments returned in the last twelve months | Rebilled share |
|---|---|---|
| 42000.00 USD | none | 100 percent |
| 42000.00 USD | 1 | no adjustment |
| 10000.00 USD | none | 100 percent |
| 9999.00 USD | none | 90 percent |
| no active certificate | none | no adjustment |

**On the boundaries.** A principal balance of exactly 10000.00 USD belongs to the first tier, the test being at least that amount. A single returned card payment inside the last twelve months takes the cardholder out of both tiers, however large the certificate. A cardholder who holds no active certificate at all meets neither tier, since both require one.
